integrity: The accompanying computations test local normalization; the universal claims rely on the written independent CRT, large-deviation, Brun--Titchmarsh and prime-progression arguments.
scientific_limitations: The exponent is not claimed sharp. The full text of Dai--Pan was inaccessible; the later Yan--Xu theorem establishes qualitative density zero, not this explicit finite-X rate. Finite enumeration cannot prove the general analytic bound.
title: Quantitative sparsity for critical-growth prime-square Romanoff sums
